correctness.rationale: Start the gap list at a designated sample label, not at the first point after a deterministic origin; translating that label to zero gives the exchangeable uniform simplex law. Two or more long gaps split the circle into runs, and a cross-run edge would traverse a long gap in either direction. With 0 or 1 long gap there is a spanning path. For k in the support of X, a specified word 1,0,…,0,1 has probability (k)₂(n−k)_{j−1}/(n)_{j+1}; multiplying by n gives exactly the normalized formula in the actual RESULT.md line 24 (no extra n). The other k values are an extension of the conditional-mean version, not positive-probability conditioning events. On the positive segment the ratio minus 1 has the sign of 2n−(j+1)k−(j−1); the zero tails and j=1 separately give the stated monotonicity properties. For the covariance, simplex translation yields q_h=(1−hr)_+^(n−1). Each run indicator has two fixed ones, j−1 fixed zeros, and n−j−1 unrestricted entries, giving the stated finite moments. The first-order term in n(q_{h+1}−q_1 q_h) is −h t² p^{h+1}; substituting into the finite sums gives Γ_j=m′_j(p)[p(1−p)−t²p²] for m_j(x)=x²(1−x)^{j−1}. The same expansion gives Var(X)=O(n), and Chebyshev with E[X] of order n makes the X=0 correction O(n⁻¹) in the density. These estimates are uniform on compact positive t ranges. Since e^t−2t>0, the variance factor is strictly positive for all t>0. Cancelling for j=1 and checking 2−(j+1)p for j≥2 gives the claimed signs and their precise limiting scope. The finite script was inspected, not executed.
